guitar.modelsText: Gibson Les Paul / Gibson ES-175 / Telecaster
guitar.evidence: Slash's Gibson Les Paul (famously a Kris Derrig replica used on Appetite for Destruction) is iconic; Izzy Stradlin's rhythm work on Telecaster/other guitars is also documented.

tone.target: hot Marshall crunch with singing lead sustain
tone.profile: hot Marshall crunch with singing lead sustain
tone.summary: A classic British crunch chain: OD boost for bite, Distortion for thick rhythm, followed by a UK 45 amp model and UK Vintage 4x12 cab to capture the iconic 'Paradise City' sound.

rig.name: Guns N' Roses - Paradise City - Valeton GP-180

blocks.purpose: Clean up hum and background noise.
Add upper-mid bite and aggressive attack for rhythm playing.
blocks.gap: No dedicated mid-hump boost, but 'Boost' is the best general option to enhance presence.

blocks.purpose: Provide thick crunch and sustain for the main rhythm parts.
blocks.gap: The 'Distortion' model is general; a dedicated Plexi/British overdrive would be ideal, but this provides the necessary grit.

blocks.purpose: Simulate the classic Marshall Plexi tone and high-gain crunch.
Provide the classic British cabinet sound and fullness.
Enhance upper-mid bite and cut low end mud.
Add subtle width and sustain to the lead lines.
blocks.gap: Not strictly necessary for the core tone, but adds dimension suitable for arena rock leads.

blocks.purpose: Add space and sustain to the lead guitar solos.
Give the overall tone a sense of large arena space.

improvements.summary: Improve cabinet realism with a specific Marshall IR to better capture the Plexi/JCM sound.

proposals.reason: Enhance the classic Marshall grit and bite missing from the current generic cab.
